content.text:
Long prompts in an open task's Prompt section in the Tasks tab are now clipped at 8 lines with a "Read more" link. A new test checks that a long prompt is clipped and expands, and that a short one has no link. The rest of the suite passes except one unrelated self-update test, which failed once in the full run and passed when run alone.

- **Clipping:** the 8 lines are counted as the prompt wraps at the tab's width. The last visible line fades into the background, and "Read more" sits beneath it in the accent colour with a down chevron.
- **Expanding:** clicking shows the whole prompt and the link becomes "Show less" with an up chevron. Clipping it again scrolls the details back to the Prompt section if you'd scrolled past it.
- **When it applies:** a prompt of 8 lines or fewer shows whole with no link, and every task opens clipped.
- **Editing a queued prompt:** it now shows as text, clipped if it's long, until you click into it. It then opens in its editor at full height while you type. A clipped prompt has to be drawn before it can be measured, which is why even a short queued prompt now needs a click before you can edit it.
- **Nothing lost:** attachments still show beneath the prompt either way, and editing always works on the whole text.

The work is in `src/prompt_mode/tasks_tab.rs`. It follows the spec, which settled on 8 lines from your 5–10 range.
